public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers are either not being built or are taking far longer than expected, so interest on their debt is piling up.

statement.excerpt: These things aren’t getting built, or if they’re getting built, it’s taking way, way longer than expected, which means that interest on that debt is piling up.
statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

from_speaker: taking way, way longer than expected
interest on that debt is piling up
our_interpretation: These things refers to the debt-financed AI data center projects discussed in the surrounding passage.
The ordinary causal reading is that material construction delays extend the period of interest incurred before facilities begin operating.

The current-state assessment uses March 1–24, 2026, the publication-month window for construction and financing updates. Earlier observations are context unless they establish a continuing condition in that window.
Longer than expected requires comparison with an original completion or delivery schedule, not simply a long construction period.
Interest accruing under normal loan terms does not alone establish additional interest caused by delay.
No company-wide accounting basis or quantified incremental interest amount is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Matched records across the referenced projects show material delays against original schedules, debt outstanding during those delays, and additional pre-operation interest attributable to the extended construction period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched records show the referenced projects broadly meeting their original schedules, or show that delays did not extend the relevant interest-bearing period or increase pre-operation interest. One successful project would not settle the broad assertion.
